title: fix: Deduplicate oracle entries in get_aggregate_price RPC
body:
## Summary

The `get_aggregate_price` RPC handler does not deduplicate oracle entries from the user-supplied `oracles` array. A caller can list the same `{account, oracle_document_id}` pair multiple times (up to 200 total entries), causing duplicate price data to be included in aggregate calculations. This makes the response's `size` field misleading and skews the mean/median/standard deviation.

## Changes

- Added a `std::set<std::pair<AccountID, std::uint32_t>>` to track seen `{account, documentID}` pairs during iteration of the oracles array
- Duplicate entries are silently skipped via `emplace().second` check, preventing the same oracle's price data from being inserted into the `Prices` bimap multiple times
- Added `#include <set>` for `std::set`

## Testing

The fix is minimal and non-breaking - duplicate entries are simply skipped after validation. Existing valid requests with unique oracles are completely unaffected. The deduplication happens after input validation, so malformed entries still return the appropriate error.

Fixes #6583

body:

-->

## High Level Overview of Change

1. Let's set CMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET to 15.0
2. Including dependencies
3. Including boost, which is kind of weird, because it uses it's own build system (b2), which is not trivial to configure
4. And document it
5. To have a nice, as good as a standard way of parsing, let's use fast_float::from_chars - it's very actively used (https://github.com/fastfloat/fast_float#users-and-related-work) and was actually included in GCC.

I checked it works on my mac (macOS 26), it works and produces no link warnings:
- natively (using Apple-Clang)
- in nix (using LLVM Clang)

I also tried to use `std::from_chars`, and it didn't build (even on my mac) - so this approach prevents us from using functions not available in older macos versions.
Can't check it builds on macOS 15, but should work.

macOS is backwards-compatible, so having older dependencies is not a problem.
And we'll even be able to build on a more modern macOS, and share the binary with an old one.

I also added a "Sanity check" - I noticed it was removed in from_chars PR.
I don't think it's needed, but just for the sake of having a peace of mind, let's have it.

UBSan suppression is not a bug - unsigned overflow is well-defined and is used inside fast_float (as well is in a ton of other libraries).

title: fix: Add null check for account object reads
body:
## High Level Overview of Change

Adds a defensive null check when `account_objects` reads ledger objects referenced by an account owner directory.

`ReadView::read` documents that it may return `nullptr` if the key is not present or the type does not match. The previous code dereferenced the returned pointer before checking it, which could crash if the directory contained an unreadable or missing object.

This change skips unreadable directory entries before accessing the SLE.

Fixes #7511

### Context of Change

Owner directories should normally reference valid ledger objects, but corrupted or inconsistent ledger state can leave a dangling directory entry. In that case, `ledger.read(keylet::child(*iter))` can return `nullptr`.

The `account_objects` handler previously used the returned pointer immediately through `sleNode->getType()` and `sleNode->getJson(...)` without checking it first. This change makes the code more defensive and avoids dereferencing a null pointer.

title: chore: Gtest migration followups first pass
body:
## High Level Overview of Change

Follow-up PR that resolves review comments left open on seven already-merged
test-migration PRs: #7136, #7133, #7054, #7046, #7317, #7304, #7292.

Those PRs were merged with a number of "let's push this to the next PR" / "keep this
convo open" threads. This audits all 72 unresolved threads across them and clears the
ones that are mechanical, plus one real bug.

**39 review threads can be resolved from this PR** — 33 fixed in code, 6 answered
without a code change (see *Deliberately not changed* below).

Test, benchmark and build files only. **No production code is touched.**

### Context of Change

The bulk is grouped into four mechanical sweeps rather than 15 scattered follow-ups,
because the same feedback recurred across PRs:
